result.final_text:
## What this letter says
Your cholesterol test was abnormal.

This is usually linked to a higher risk of stroke and heart attack.

Your doctor thinks your levels are high. Treatment is the next best step.

Diet only lowers cholesterol a little. With a strict diet, most people can lower it by 15%.

If cholesterol is moderately to severely high, diet is usually not the first treatment.

Most of the time, high cholesterol comes from your genes. It does not depend on diet.

Diabetes or hypertension adds to your risk when cholesterol is high (hypercholesterolemia).

New research says treating high cholesterol can lower the risk of Alzheimer's disease.

The letter does not give your cholesterol numbers. A copy of your lab results is enclosed.

The letter names no medicine. It does not say what treatments you could have, other than diet.

## What you need to do
1. Think about calling to make a follow-up appointment. It is about your cholesterol.
2. Your doctor asks you to make one if you want treatment.
3. If you have more questions, you can contact your doctor.

## Dates and medicines
- Dates: the letter gives no dates.
- Medicines: the letter names no medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What do my cholesterol numbers mean?
- What treatment choices do I have?
- What does hypertension mean?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
